headline: High risk: Goose can write/egress by default while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs list, so interaction risks are mostly one-sided but include prompt-injection and data-leakage via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is a docs-only list with no runtime surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest Goose output. But Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and uses MCP/extensions, so if the user copies list content into files or an MCP source, Goose can treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise pathway exists, but only through shared files or manual bridging.
conditions: IF the user places untrusted text from awesome-nlp into a file Goose reads as instructions, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF Goose is connected to an MCP server that forwards content from the list without provenance, THEN instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp content read-only and never feed it into Goose prompts.
Disable or remove untrusted MCP servers for the session.
Use a separate workspace directory for Goose.
Add a manual review step before Goose acts on file content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no execution surface, but Goose reads files in the cwd, writes the filesystem, and has broad network egress plus model-provider calls. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, Goose can transmit them to third-party services. The risk is driven by Goose; awesome-nlp is only relevant as a possible source of shared files.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Goose's working directory, THEN Goose can read and exfiltrate them via network egress.
IF the user stores secrets in files referenced by awesome-nlp content, THEN Goose may transmit those secrets to model providers.
mitigations: Move secrets out of Goose's workspace.
Run Goose in a dedicated directory with non-sensitive files only.
Disable network egress where possible.
Rotate any secrets that were already placed in the shared workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss prevention.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write, shell, git, or network capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally with Goose. Goose does have unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git modification, but there is no second writer on the pair. The only overlap is read-only documentation content, so the conflict surface is minimal.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp is treated as a live agent rather than a static list, THEN the assumption breaks, but that capability is not present in the profile.
IF another writable agent is added to the same directory, THEN write conflicts could emerge.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp as a static reference only.
Avoid running multiple Goose instances against the same repo.
Use separate git branches per session.
Pause before committing Goose-generated changes.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is static documentation, so it does not generate actions. Goose, however, can act on file and MCP inputs and has shell and git authority. If Goose consumes content derived from the list as authoritative guidance, it may propagate errors into code or commands without verification. The pathway is indirect but plausible because Goose is action-capable.
conditions: IF Goose uses text copied from awesome-nlp as authoritative instructions, THEN downstream mistakes can be committed or executed.
IF Goose is allowed to act without a human review step, THEN erroneous guidance can cascade into shell or git actions.
mitigations: Require human review before Goose executes commands.
Cross-check any guidance from awesome-nlp against primary sources.
Use Goose in dry-run mode for high-impact actions.
Limit Goose to non-production repositories.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before shell or git actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is declared for awesome-nlp, so there is no direct residency or retention issue on that side. Goose handles source code and files in cwd and may send them to configured model providers, which can create policy mismatch if regulated data is placed there. The other agent is not cited for compliance because it has no data handling surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Goose's workspace, THEN provider-side processing may violate local policy.
IF the workspace contains data subject to retention limits, THEN Goose's external calls may conflict with those limits.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose's workspace.
Review provider and retention settings before use.
Use a separate environment for compliance-sensitive projects.
Delete temporary files after each session.
requires-engineering: configure policy-based data routing and retention controls.
